item.title: Pro-democracy activists increasingly vulnerable to authoritarian governments in Southeast Asia
item.description: Activists across Asia are being hunted down by authoritarian governments even across international borders. Human rights groups have been warning of a "swap market" of repression in Southeast Asia.

item.title: What a Pearly King taught me about Cockney rhyming slang and East London history
item.description: In mother-of-pearl suits, the Pearly Kings used to canvass East London for charity. The most famous one, George Major, died in August. A look back on this larger-than-life figure and the Pearly King tradition.

item.title: Israel's prime minister says a pilot tried to crash a plane traveling to Tel Aviv
item.description: One pilot stabbed another pilot on a FlyDubai flight headed to Tel Aviv on Wednesday and may have tried to crash the plane before passengers and crew members subdued him, Israel's prime minister says.

item.title: Picanha, prices and politics: What Brazil's favorite steak says about the election
item.description: President Lula promised Brazilians four years ago they'd be able to afford picanha again. Now, as he seeks another term, the price of the country's favorite cut of beef is telling a different story.

item.description: Kimberly Prost, a Canadian judge at the International Criminal Court, says U.S. sanctions disrupted her daily life. She is still hearing cases and challenging the sanctions in court.

item.title: Swiss glaciers suffer another year of record ice loss
item.description: Switzerland's glaciers are disappearing at a record pace. More than 5% of their ice has vanished this year alone — threatening water supplies, ecosystems and communities across Europe.

item.title: How Ukrainians are coping with new, more deadly Russian attacks
item.description: Zanny Minton Beddoes, The Economist's editor in chief, just visited Ukraine. She says, despite all its drone weaponry, Kyiv is under extraordinary bombardment, as Russia tries to make it unlivable.
